seed_fields.description: Predict a single aligned floating output with bounded Keras batching. Model must be a caller-provisioned tf_keras.Model. Inputs are a nonempty list/tuple of finite float32/float64 arrays sharing a nonzero leading dimension. Preserve native Keras conversion, row order and partial batches. Require an explicit positive Python integer batch_size, excluding bool. Return one finite floating ndarray with the same leading dimension. No fitting, model loading, domain feature transformation or unit conversion occurs. Arbitrary custom model code remains caller-trusted; this operation is not a sandbox or a model authenticity check. Only concrete provisioned execution is supported. Caller limits model-compute threads and reserves one additional private dataset worker; dataset autotuning is disabled.

interfaces.name: model
interfaces.constraints: Caller-provisioned trusted legacy-Keras model in the qualified installed runtime. Model input geometry, custom code, state authenticity, feature meanings and units remain caller responsibilities. No model loading or fitting is performed. Custom predict/model code is not sandboxed; automatic graph/cache creation can occur.

interfaces.name: inputs
interfaces.constraints: Nonempty list or tuple of finite float32/float64 arrays, each rank>=1, sharing a nonzero leading dimension N. Preserve caller row and input order. Native Keras conversion remains in effect; model-defined input geometry and dtype conversion are not inferred by this provider. Inputs and model are private in-process runtime values.

interfaces.name: batch_size
interfaces.constraints: Positive Python integer excluding bool. Explicit native Keras batch size, including the final partial batch. Caller bounds model-compute threads and reserves one additional private dataset worker. Dataset autotuning is disabled. Batch size does not independently bound memory or model-compute concurrency.

interfaces.name: result
interfaces.constraints: One finite floating numpy.ndarray with rank>=1 and leading dimension N matching input rows. Remaining shape, output dtype and units follow the caller model. Multiple outputs, nonfinite output and row-count mismatch are rejected after prediction. No feature preparation, key joining, loss, confidence calibration or unit conversion. Concrete provisioned execution only; abstract witness rejects. No JSON/HTTP transport, clean-install or empirical effectiveness qualification. Synthetic motion and electrical-power examples establish constructed reuse, and a full-size B5 check establishes native batch parity.

limitations: Draft plan only; transaction, semantic review and publication gates remain required.
TensorFlow and legacy Keras are software dependencies, not registered atom dependencies. The matcher helper is separately hash-bound.
Caller-provisioned custom model code remains trusted and may have side effects; this is not arbitrary-code isolation.
The bounded prediction operation does not qualify image-model training, the complete OSIC workflow or empirical transfer.
